regime_context: The detector shows a broad, two-horse race in Canada: Base Metals & Copper and Oil & Gas Producers both carry positive, eligible momentum scores at the top of the ranks, with the rest of the board largely flat or negative. Breadth of rotation is wide (56% eligible), absorption is low, and no single narrative dominates — this is a diffuse commodity-led tape, not a clean one-theme regime. The trend gate has historically helped control drawdown on this market, but cross-sectional momentum has near-zero rank-IC, so I treat the ranks purely as a focus lens.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Oil & Gas overtakes Base Metals as the confirmed leader: I would retire this watch if XEG.TO closes at a higher detector score than XBM.TO for 5 consecutive trading days with Oil & Gas still eligible under the absolute-trend gate.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas sits at rank 2 with a score only marginally behind the leader and carries the highest durability bar (0.61) plus a 'mixed' Hurst tag, which is the strongest trend-health combination among the top eligible names. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated leg on this market and Oil & Gas is eligible under it, so the risk-control discipline supports staying with the theme rather than the rank. Crowding is muted (z ~0.97), so there is no size-down caution from that leg.
theses.dissent: Commodity leadership in Canada has been choppy and mean-reverting historically, and Oil & Gas sits directly behind a leader that itself shows a mean-revert Hurst tag — the whole commodity complex could rotate lower together on a broad risk-off or demand scare.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO lags XBM.TO by more than 5% over the next 10 trading days while the absolute-trend gate flips Oil & Gas to ineligible

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals is the outright leader with the highest score and a wide breadth reading (0.556), but its Hurst tag is 'mean-revert' and its durability bar is only 0.50 — meaning the leadership may be less sticky than the rank suggests. The trend gate is the only validated edge and it is currently satisfied, so staying with the leader is defensible on risk-control grounds, not on momentum. Crowding is not elevated (z 0.9), so no size-down signal.
theses.dissent: The 'mean-revert' Hurst tag is exactly the failure mode for trend-following in Canada — leadership that reverts quickly can hand back gains faster than a 'trend' or 'mixed' tag would, and the momentum rank itself has near-zero forward IC.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 5% over any rolling 10-day window while the trend gate stays green

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is the only theme flagged crowded (true, z 1.16) while carrying a negative score and a 'mixed' Hurst tag. The crowding flag is explicitly a size-down caution, never a fade, but combined with negative momentum and eligibility it leaves no positive reason to hold an overweight view. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated leg and Technology barely clears it (eligible=true but score -0.21), so the risk-control case is weak.
theses.dissent: Crowding can persist far longer than expected and an 'avoid' call on a crowded name risks missing a continuation if the narrative re-accelerates; the theme is still eligible under the trend gate, so it is not broken.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO closes in the top 3 by score for 10 consecutive trading days while its crowding z falls below 0.5
